audit_comment: THE DRAGON ISSUE-10 OPENER ROUND, PART TWO - three adjudicated chains and the part-one flip. The Gilbert Let There Be A Method To Your Madness article (folios 11-14): the builders-mindset doctrine with the organized-origins rule, the misread-rooms doctrine, the builder-traits decree, the storage-room rule, the two-views drawing scale at 200 feet to the inch, the keep-it-simple doctrine, the rich-builder doctrine and the Nappo example - 120 years of life, 275 years dead, three facets generating fifteen levels. The Crabaugh Weights & Measures article (folios 19-20): the 3d6 Size and d6 Build with the hit-per-die bonuses at 16 and penalties at 5, the pound at 10 GP, the armor fractions at 15, 30 and 60 percent of body mass, the female +2 Constitution and +1 Dexterity, the carrying-capacity grid in tenths with the elf column mirroring the human, the speed ladder at 3, 6, 9 and 12, the male and female height-and-weight grids across the sixteen Size rows, and the appearance bands - eyes, hair, skin, voice, handedness, expression and hair length, males at 30% bearded. The Holsinger Gaining a New Experience Level article (folios 20-21): the four-part ritual, the sacrifice total at double the new level with each creature at least half, the conscious-sacrifice rule, the 50/50 and 60/40 notice chances with the 50% temple-rite kill, the mistletoe and tree sacrifices at 10 and 1 hit dice, the drunken-stupor emissaries, the demihuman liquor toughness, the 7th-level militia ejection and the guild halls, and the spell learning and forgetting rules. The part-one box in report 010 flips closed (1 closed / 1 open).

banner.title: The Dragon issue-10 opener, part two - the Gilbert dungeon method article (folios 11-14), the Weights & Measures article (folios 19-20) and the Holsinger level ritual article (folios 20-21): three adjudicated chains and the part-one flip
banner.provenance: Pinned from The Dragon Vol. 2 No. 4 (October 1977), the archive.org scan voice (single-voice; the source lives in the archive.org item accessory-dragon-magazine-012). The folios: 11-14, the Gilbert Design Forum dungeon-method article - think like the builders and allow every necessary function, the organized society that dug the dungeon out of solid rock and then abandoned it, the rooms no longer used for their intention and read like antedated storefronts, the builder occupation, standing, alignment and personality decreeing the levels, the storage-room rule, the two views - vertical cutaway and horizontal overlay at 200 feet to the inch - keep it simple and stick to a plan, the rich-builder doctrine, and the Nappo dig: 120 years of life, 275 years dead, three facets and fifteen levels, the report 010 box label reading 11-13 against the article tail riding folio 14 beside the Archive ad; 19-20, the Crabaugh Weights & Measures article - Size on 3d6 and Build on d6, +1 hit per die at Size 16 and up, -1 at 5 and down, one pound at 10 GP, armor at 15, 30 and 60 percent of body mass, females +2 Constitution and +1 Dexterity with the lighter carrying capacity, the musculature-versus-force doctrine, the carrying grid - human 1.0 to 3.0, dwarf 1.5 to 3.5, hobbit 2.0 to 4.0 in tenths of body weight, the elf column mirroring the human, the speed ladder at 3, 6, 9 and 12, the male height-and-weight grid from 5-1 and 120 pounds to 6-4 and 215, the female grid from 4-10 and 100 to 6-1 and 185, and the appearance bands - eyes, hair, skin, voice, handedness, expression, hair length, males at 30 percent bearded; 20-21, the Holsinger Gaining a New Experience Level article - the four-part ritual of qualification, attention, intercession and exhaustion, the good fasting and prayer or the sacrifice at double the new level with each creature at least half and conscious, the 50/50 neutral notice and the 50/50 evil nothing, the 60/40 sacrilege chances and the 50% temple-rite kill, the druid tree at 1 hit die and mistletoe at 10, the neutral mistletoe tree rite with its free cure, the Great Pink Elephants in the drunken stupor, the demihuman liquor toughness behind the level limits, the 7th-level militia ejection and the guild halls, and the spell learning by the Greyhawk columns with one forgettable spell per level. The part-one box in report 010 flips closed this round, 1 closed / 1 open. PRINT FOLIO = PDF PAGE, verified at the printed 10, 19 and 21 footers.
banner.sentinel: The variant-layer doctrine holds: Dragon ink is never core 1e canon, and the Holsinger level ritual and the Crabaugh Size system - though both echo later print - pin as a variant layer with provenance, never core canon. The print quirks ride AS SCANNED, noted, never silent: the male medium-weight Size-4 cell reading 185 as scanned against the 135 column pattern; the female Size-15 height cell garbled and riding sentinel -1; the carrying grid elf column mirroring the human with its two garbled cells riding the transcript, the dwarf Strength-16 cell garbled and riding sentinel; the speed-12 fraction garbled in the OCR, the speed pinning and the fraction riding; the facial-features d6-minus-2 rule and the limb tables riding prose; the Snits game and the Stellar Conquest article scoped out as other systems. The editor's standing caution rides: none of this is official.

consts.name: dtnGilNappoLevels
consts.comment: the Nappo dig example - three personality facets generated fifteen levels, the builder assumed celibate and a recluse (folios 12-14)

consts.name: dtnGilNappoFacets
consts.comment: the Nappo example facets - an MU, fond of animal experimentation, needing space for his orcs (folios 12-14)

consts.name: dtnGilScaleFtPerInch
consts.comment: the two-views drawing scale - 200 feet to the inch, or whatever fits one sheet (folio 13)

consts.name: dtnGilNappoLifespanYears
consts.comment: Nappo, assisted by magic, lived on the site for 120 years (folio 12)

consts.name: dtnGilNappoDeadYears
consts.comment: the 275 years since Nappo died, his orcs continuing to inhabit the place (folio 12)

consts.name: dtnWmPoundGp
consts.comment: one pound is presumed to equal 10 GP (folio 19)

consts.name: dtnWmLeatherPct
consts.comment: armor weight as a fraction of body mass - leather armor 15% (folio 19)

consts.name: dtnWmChainPct
consts.comment: chain mail weighs 30% of body mass (folio 19)

consts.name: dtnWmPlatePct
consts.comment: plate mail weighs 60% of body mass (folio 19)

consts.name: dtnWmFemaleConBonus
consts.comment: females add 2 to their Constitution score (folio 19)

consts.name: dtnWmFemaleDexBonus
consts.comment: females add 1 to their Dexterity score (folio 19)

consts.name: dtnWmSizeBonusMin
consts.comment: a Size of 16 or greater adds 1 hit per die (folio 19)

consts.name: dtnWmSizePenaltyMax
consts.comment: a Size of 5 or less subtracts 1 hit per die (folio 19)

consts.name: dtnWmSizeHpMod
consts.comment: the Size hit-per-die modification (folio 19)

consts.name: dtnWmSpeedFull
consts.comment: at maximum carrying capacity the character staggers along at speed 3 (folio 20)

consts.name: dtnWmSpeedTwoThirds
consts.comment: at two-thirds maximum the character moves at speed 6 (folio 20)

consts.name: dtnWmSpeedOneThird
consts.comment: at one-third maximum the character moves at speed 9 (folio 20)

consts.name: dtnWmSpeedLightest
consts.comment: at the lightest fraction the character moves at speed 12 - the printed fraction garbled in the OCR and riding the transcript (folio 20)

consts.name: dtnWmMaleBeardPct
consts.comment: males have a 30% chance of having a beard (folio 20)

consts.name: dtnWmSizeBands
consts.comment: the Size range - 3 through 18 on 3d6, sixteen rows per height and weight table (folio 19)

consts.name: dtnWmCarryBands
consts.comment: the carrying-capacity Strength range - 3 through 18, sixteen rows (folio 20)

consts.name: dtnHolsSacrificeTotalFactor
consts.comment: the sacrifice total - hit dice double the number of the new experience level (folio 20)

consts.name: dtnHolsSacrificeEachMinHalf
consts.comment: each individual creature must have at least half as many hit dice as the new level (folio 20)

consts.name: dtnHolsNeutralSacrificePct
consts.comment: a neutral sacrifice without a cleric - 50/50 the good gods or the evil gods notice (folio 20)

consts.name: dtnHolsEvilSacrificeNothingPct
consts.comment: an evil sacrifice without a good cleric - 50/50 that nothing happens (folio 20)

consts.name: dtnHolsGoodSacrilegeRightPct
consts.comment: sacrilege against the good gods without clerics - a 60% chance the right gods notice (folio 21)

consts.name: dtnHolsWrongGodsPct
consts.comment: a 40% chance the wrong gods notice at sacrilege against the good gods (folio 21)

consts.name: dtnHolsTempleRiteKillPct
consts.comment: a rite of a different alignment in an outraged temple - a 50% chance the gods show up immediately and kill, no chance for revival (folio 21)

consts.name: dtnHolsCastleLevel
consts.comment: characters usually build their own castle in the wilderness at the 7th experience level (folio 21)

consts.name: dtnHolsTreeHD
consts.comment: the druid-appeased sacrifice of a tree counts as a one-hit-die neutral creature (folio 21)

consts.name: dtnHolsMistletoeHD
consts.comment: mistletoe counts as ten hit dice (folio 21)

consts.name: dtnHolsTreeMinFt
consts.comment: the sacrificed tree must be at least ten feet tall and alive - potted - when sacrificed in a temple (folio 21)

bools.name: dtnGilBuildersMindset
bools.comment: the designer must think like the builders and allow for all the necessary functions of the dungeon (folio 11)

bools.name: dtnGilOrganizedOrigins
bools.comment: dungeons are abandoned by the organized society it required to build them - digging one out of solid rock is a tremendous task (folio 11)

bools.name: dtnGilRoomsMisread
bools.comment: the rooms are no longer used for what they were intended - players read them like antedated storefronts by torchlight and never guess (folios 12-13)

bools.name: dtnGilBuilderTraitsDecree
bools.comment: the builder occupation, social standing, alignment and personality decree a great number of levels for his own personal use (folios 11-12)

bools.name: dtnGilStorageRoomsRule
bools.comment: always allow for storage rooms in the levels - it was a long hike to the surface (folio 12)

bools.name: dtnGilTwoViewsRule
bools.comment: draw two views of the dungeon as a whole - a vertical cutaway and a horizontal overlay, both to scale, the levels as rectangles with their purpose written in (folio 13)

bools.name: dtnGilKeepItSimple
bools.comment: keep it simple and stick to a plan - what looks obvious on paper is the deepest of forbidden mysteries to the players (folio 12)

bools.name: dtnGilRichBuilderRichDungeon
bools.comment: the more a builder is developed, the more rich and varied his dungeons - each trait of character finds expression in additional levels (folios 13-14)

bools.name: dtnWmSizeThreeDice
bools.comment: Size is an additional characteristic rolled on 3 six-sided dice (folio 19)

bools.name: dtnWmBuildFunctionalHumans
bools.comment: Build rolls on one six-sided die - 1 light, 2-5 normal, 6 heavy - functional only for humans but rolled for non-humans anyway (folio 19)

bools.name: dtnWmElfMirrorsHuman
bools.comment: the carrying-capacity elf column mirrors the human column by the print own arithmetic - the strength-5 and strength-16 cells garbled in the OCR and riding the transcript (folio 20)

bools.name: dtnWmFemaleLighterCapacity
bools.comment: females sit at a carrying-capacity disadvantage through body mass, with no Strength penalty (folio 20)

bools.name: dtnWmMusculatureVsForce
bools.comment: two kinds of strength - how well muscled, reflected in the Strength characteristic, and physical force, reflected in carrying capacity as a multiple of body weight (folio 20)

bools.name: dtnWmAppearanceHumanOnly
bools.comment: the appearance tables are intended for humans and work poorly to not at all for non-humans (folio 20)

bools.name: dtnHolsFourPartRitual
bools.comment: the four parts of gaining a level - qualifying experience, attracting the gods, a cleric intercession, complete exhaustion (folio 20)

bools.name: dtnHolsGoodFastingPrayer
bools.comment: the good attract the gods by fasting and prayer in a temple - no danger from other gods, but a substantial free-will offering required (folio 20)

bools.name: dtnHolsSacrificeConsciousRule
bools.comment: sacrifices must be conscious and not under the influence of magic (folio 20)

bools.name: dtnHolsGoodNoNeutralHumans
bools.comment: good may not sacrifice neutral humans though they may sacrifice evil humans - evil may sacrifice both (folio 21)

bools.name: dtnHolsNeutralMistletoeRite
bools.comment: the neutral rite - getting laid while perched in a mistletoe tree, the druids paid, a free cure light wounds for the stickers (folio 21)

bools.name: dtnHolsClericIntercession
bools.comment: a cleric of the character own alignment must intercede so only the gods of that alignment show up (folio 20)

bools.name: dtnHolsClericsExpectPay
bools.comment: clerics expect to be paid for their services throughout the ritual (folio 20)

bools.name: dtnHolsExhaustionStuporRule
bools.comment: the only reliable attitude is complete exhaustion - thoroughly inebriated following great physical activity, whereupon the Emissaries of the Gods, the Great Pink Elephants, lay on the new abilities (folio 21)

bools.name: dtnHolsDemiHumanLiquorToughness
bools.comment: dwarves, elves and hobbits are tougher to get bombed - this is why there are limits on the experience levels they may reach (folio 21)

bools.name: dtnHolsMilitiaEjects7th
bools.comment: the local militia heaves passed-out characters over the town walls at the 7th level, whence the wilderness castle (folio 21)

bools.name: dtnHolsGuildHalls
bools.comment: cities contain guild halls for each profession where members carouse in safety, even mass affairs promoting dozens at once (folio 21)

bools.name: dtnHolsSpellLearningRitual
bools.comment: new spell levels are learned from the Great Pink Elephants by the Greyhawk minimum-per-level column with percentile rolls against the chance to know any given spell (folio 21)

bools.name: dtnHolsForgettingSpells
bools.comment: each new level a character may choose to forget one spell of each level previously known, to make room for others (folio 21)
